abstract:
Research has shown that free-form
            Game-Design (GD)
            environments can be very effective in fostering
            Computational Thinking (CT)
            skills at a young age. However, some students can still need some guidance during the learning process due to the highly open-ended nature of these environments.
            Intelligent Pedagogical Agents (IPAs)
            can be used to provide personalized assistance in real-time to alleviate this challenge. This paper presents our results in evaluating such an agent deployed in a real-word free-form GD learning environment to foster CT in the early K-12 education, Unity-CT. We focus on the effect of repetition by comparing student behaviors between no intervention, 1-shot, and repeated intervention groups for two different errors that are known to be challenging in the online lessons of Unity-CT. Our findings showed that the agent was perceived very positively by the students and the repeated intervention showed promising results in terms of helping students make fewer errors and more correct behaviors, albeit only for one of the two target errors. Building from these results, we provide insights on how to provide IPA interventions in free-form GD environments.

ur.tldr: 在开放式游戏设计学习环境中评估教学智能体，比较无干预、单次与重复干预对两类错误的影响；学生整体评价积极，重复干预可减少部分错误并促进正确行为，但效果依错误类型而异。

title: The Impact of Intelligent Pedagogical Agents’ Interventions on Student Behavior and Performance in Open-Ended Game Design Environments
